Carlos De La Cruz

Republican candidate for U.S. Representative, District 35, Bexar County, Texas · Open seat

Retired U.S. Air Force veteran and San Antonio small-business owner (co-founded a kickboxing gym)

Carlos De La Cruz, 46, is a Republican candidate for the redrawn 35th Congressional District, which covers south, east and northeast Bexar County plus Guadalupe, Karnes and Wilson counties. He served 20 years in the U.S. Air Force and later co-founded a kickboxing gym in San Antonio with his wife. He finished second in the 11-candidate March 3, 2026 Republican primary, then defeated state Rep. John Lujan in the May 26 runoff, and faces Democrat Johnny Garcia on November 3.

Where Cruz stands

Economy and inflation
Proposes cutting federal spending without reducing benefits retirees have earned, expanding American energy production to lower costs, and reducing regulations on small businesses.
Taxes
Says he supports pro-growth tax policy and cutting wasteful spending so that small businesses can compete.
Border security and immigration
Supports funding border infrastructure, personnel and technology, expanding legal authority for border officials, and pursuing cartels. Also supports reforming what he calls a backlogged legal immigration system.
Health care
Supports more market competition, price transparency, more coverage options for small businesses and self-employed workers, and less regulation for rural clinics. Also supports incentives for medical professionals to work in underserved areas.
Public safety
Supports full backing for law enforcement and going after cartels he says are bringing fentanyl into communities.
Congress and executive power
Says Congress should actively pass laws rather than rely on executive action, because laws last longer. Says he plans to work with President Trump and congressional leaders to advance their agenda.

Background

  • U.S. Air Force, 20 years (enlisted at 18); deployed to the Middle East after 9/11 and did drug-interdiction work at the southern border
  • Co-founder and owner, with his wife Annette, of a kickboxing gym in San Antonio
  • Has not held elected office
  • 2026: placed second in the March 3 Republican primary for TX-35; won the May 26 runoff against John Lujan
  • Endorsed by President Donald Trump on February 16, 2026
  • Brother of U.S. Rep. Monica De La Cruz (R-TX-15)
